risks.title: Macroeconomic Conditions
risks.score_rationale: Consumer confidence and economic conditions directly impact demand for recreational vehicles. The company is exposed to market fluctuations and changes in economic conditions, with a noted negative impact during fiscal year 2025.

risks.title: Tariffs
risks.score_rationale: Tariffs can have a significant impact on the company's production costs and sales, particularly in the context of international trade. Uncertainty regarding the future impact of tariffs is high.

risks.title: Interest Rates and Financing
risks.score_rationale: Higher interest rates compared to recent years have had a negative impact on wholesale and retail demand during fiscal year 2025. This affects both independent dealers and end consumers.

risks.title: Dealer Inventory
risks.score_rationale: Independent RV dealer inventory in North America decreased by 2.3% to 73,300 units. Dealers are closely evaluating the inventory levels they wish to maintain based on retail activity and financing costs.

risks.title: Environmental Regulation
risks.score_rationale: Environmental regulation can impact the company's production costs and sales, particularly regarding greenhouse gas emissions. The company must be prepared to adapt to regulatory changes.

risks.title: Competition in the RV Sector
risks.score_rationale: Competition in the recreational vehicle sector is high. Even with a dominant market share of 39.1%, the company must innovate and improve its products to remain competitive.

risks.title: Tax Reform (OBBB)
risks.score_rationale: The One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) signed on July 4, 2025 includes several tax reform provisions including 100% bonus depreciation, research and development expenses, and limitations on interest expense deductions. The net impact for fiscal year 2025 stems from bonus depreciation for assets placed in service after January 19, 2025.
